metadata.title: This Week: What's Done, What's Next
metadata.register: Professional, polite, simple -- a real progress update, not overhyped, per the user's explicit tone request.
metadata.note: A CLI-explainer weekly recap -- a NEW week's log, separate from the earlier weekly-recap, weekly-recap-catbot, weekly-recap-suffolk and weekly-recap-never-forgets builds. Same story spine as those builds (B00 cold open -> problem -> ask -> code -> output -> change -> code -> output -> lesson -> handoff -> outro; real code shown via ClaudeCodeBeat; one required revision cycle). weekly_recap_v1.py and weekly_recap_v2.py are genuine Python scripts, both actually run; v1 is a flat list of three entries, v2 splits it into DONE THIS WEEK (three items) and NEXT (the lecture itself, Tuesday). Unlike the Suffolk recap, the lecture presentation is FINISHED this week, so it sits under DONE and only the delivery is NEXT. Disclosed substitutions carried forward: (1) af_bella + @HumanitariansAI instead of the skill's default voice/handle, per the user's earlier explicit requests; (2) rendered through run.sh/compile.py/static_scene_check.py/manim_layout_audit.py/final_frame_check.py, the pipeline used on every reel this session. Self-intro ('Hi, I'm Agrima') folds into B00's own narration, per the cli-explainer skill's convention and the earlier weekly-recap builds. The college is deliberately NOT named (the user said only 'a college'); no lecture date beyond 'this Tuesday', no slide count and no attendance are stated. All items are the user's own self-reported account. No footage exists -- every visual is a generated Manim graphic: an article-header card, a four-video grid, a lecture-slide card and a Tuesday card.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat -- the ACTUAL code; weekly_recap_v1.py was really run
beats.narration_text: Here's the first version. A flat list with three entries: the article, the videos, and the lecture, all in one row.

props.title: weekly_recap_v1.py
props.code:
WEEK = [
    {"item": "Published 'The Tutor They Never Had' on Substack",
     "where": "AI tutoring for kids who have never had extra help"},
    {"item": "Produced four Brutalist videos (16:9 + 9:16 each)",
     "where": "planning, review, approvals, export"},
    {"item": "Guest lecture on Humanitarians AI -- with Yatra",
     "where": "presentation finished; lecture is Tuesday"},
]

def log():
    for entry in WEEK:
        print(f"- {entry['item']}  ({entry['where']})")

beats.role_note: the real weekly_recap_v1.py output, visualized as three same-weight cards
beats.narration_text: Run it, and here's the week. One article, The Tutor They Never Had, published on Substack, about how AI tutoring could help children who have never had extra help. Four Brutalist videos, each taken through planning, review, approvals, and export, in both sixteen by nine and nine by sixteen. And a guest lecture on Humanitarians AI at a college, with Yatra, where the presentation is now finished.
beats.visual_intent: three same-weight cards in a row: Substack article card, four-video grid, lecture-presentation card

beats.role_note: the revision ask -- split done from next
beats.narration_text: But a flat list treats a finished article the same as a lecture that hasn't happened yet. So the next ask was to split it: what's done, and what's next.

props.title: weekly_recap_v2.py
props.code:
DONE = [
    {"item": "Published 'The Tutor They Never Had' on Substack",
     "where": "AI tutoring for kids who have never had extra help"},
    {"item": "Produced four Brutalist videos (16:9 + 9:16 each)",
     "where": "planning, review, approvals, export"},
    {"item": "Finished the guest-lecture presentation",
     "where": "Humanitarians AI, with Yatra"},
]

NEXT = [
    {"item": "Deliver the guest lecture at a college -- Tuesday",
     "where": "alongside Yatra"},
]

def log():
    print("DONE THIS WEEK")
    ...
    print("NEXT")
    ...

beats.role_note: the real weekly_recap_v2.py output, visualized: DONE (three cards) vs NEXT (Tuesday lecture card)
beats.narration_text: Re-run it, and the picture is clearer. Done this week: the article is published, all four videos are finished in both formats, and the lecture presentation is ready. Next: the lecture itself, this Tuesday, alongside Yatra. That part hasn't happened yet, and I'd rather say so plainly.
beats.visual_intent: three small DONE cards on the left, one NEXT card (Tuesday lecture) on the right, separated by a divider

beats.narration_text: So that's the real update: one article published, four videos produced, a presentation ready, and one lecture ahead on Tuesday. Keeping done and next apart is a small habit, but it keeps a recap honest.
beats.visual_intent: typographic card: 'Done from next. / Not a small detail. / The whole difference.'
